caustica.options.rt.exposureMode.tooltip: How the ray-traced image is mapped to display brightness. Auto adapts to scene luminance; Manual uses the exposure value directly.
caustica.options.rt.manualEv.tooltip: Exposure compensation in stops. In Manual, this is the fixed exposure. In Auto, this biases the auto exposure brighter or darker.
caustica.options.rt.gamma.tooltip: Post-transform luminance gamma. Values below 1.00 brighten shadows and midtones while preserving black, white, and color ratios.
caustica.options.rt.spp.tooltip: Path-tracing samples taken per pixel each frame. Higher is cleaner but more demanding.
caustica.options.rt.maxBounces.tooltip: Maximum number of secondary path-tracing bounces after the primary hit. Higher captures more indirect light but costs more.
caustica.options.rt.entities.tooltip: Include entities and block entities in the ray-traced scene.
caustica.options.rt.particles.tooltip: Draw particles as camera-ray billboards inside the traced scene.
caustica.options.rt.glow.tooltip: Draw the vanilla Glowing-effect outline (through walls) around glowing entities.
caustica.options.rt.waterWaves.tooltip: Animate water-surface normals for moving wave highlights.
caustica.options.rt.cloudDensity.tooltip: Multiplier on the volumetric cloud layer's density. Lower values make the same cloud shapes thinner and more translucent, so light penetrates deeper and the deck's depth becomes visible; higher values close the clouds into a denser, more opaque deck.
caustica.options.rt.motionBlur.tooltip: Blur the image along each pixel's real motion vectors over the shutter interval. Camera turns and moving objects streak the way a film camera's open shutter does; cost is one display-resolution pass.
caustica.options.rt.motionBlurShutter.to: How much of the frame interval the virtual shutter stays open, in degrees: 180 is the film standard (half the frame), 360 keeps it open the whole time, 0 disables the streak.
caustica.options.rt.motionBlurSamples.to: Taps averaged along the streak. More is smoother on fast motion; 8 is a good default.
caustica.options.rt.hdr.tooltip: Recreate the swapchain for HDR (ST.2084/PQ) or native SDR output. Applied at the next frame boundary.
caustica.options.rt.hdrUiBrightness.tool: Absolute brightness (in nits) assigned to SDR-authored UI on an HDR display. BT.2408 puts SDR graphics white at 203 nits; the ACES HDR output transform puts a white surface in the world near 107 nits at a 1000 nit peak.
caustica.options.rt.hdrPeak.tooltip: Absolute brightness (in nits) highlights roll off toward, and the peak the HDR mastering metadata declares. Set to your display's peak HDR brightness.
caustica.options.rt.denoiser.tooltip: Which denoiser cleans up the path-traced image. Auto picks the best one this machine can run. DLSS Ray Reconstruction needs an NVIDIA RTX GPU, NRD needs its native library, and the built-in denoiser always works but is softer because it has no frame history. Off shows the raw traced image.
caustica.options.rt.superResolutionMetho: Which upscaler brings the render-resolution image to your screen. Auto uses FSR when its runtime is installed and the built-in bilinear resolve otherwise. Bilinear always works but is softer.
caustica.options.rt.superResolution.tool: Render resolution the world is traced at before being scaled to your screen. Lower modes render fewer pixels and scale more aggressively for higher framerates; higher modes render more pixels for a sharper image. DLSS Ray Reconstruction uses its own equivalent modes.
caustica.options.rt.debugView.tooltip: Inspect ray-tracing buffers and exposure diagnostics after the normal frame has rendered.
caustica.options.rt.depthOfField.tooltip: Trace the primary rays through the camera aperture so out-of-focus content blurs the way a real lens does. The Field of View option sets the focal length, so a narrow FOV focuses tighter at the same aperture and focus distance.
caustica.options.rt.dofMode.tooltip: How the out-of-focus blur is produced. Simple gathers a circle of confusion from the finished image: it is stable and cheap, and a sharp foreground is composited over a defocused background rather than smeared into it. Physical makes the primary rays leave through the camera aperture, so the blur is real bokeh of the lens, at the cost of rays and of visible sampling at wide apertures.
caustica.options.rt.dofArtisticBlur.tool: How much of the lens' own blur the artistic mode draws. 1.0x is the aperture exactly: the focal length, f-number and focus distance decide where the sharp band falls, so focusing far away keeps the whole picture sharp and opening the aperture softens the background. Raise it to exaggerate the effect past what the lens would do, lower it for a gentler one.
caustica.options.rt.dofMaxBlur.tooltip: Largest disc the physical and simple modes treat as sharp, as a percentage of the frame height. It sets how deep the depth of field is rather than how strong the blur is: raise it and more of the frame stays within the disc and reads as sharp, lower it and the sharp band tightens around the focal plane.
caustica.options.rt.dofSamples.tooltip: Points of the aperture each pixel traces through. The trace covers only a small disc of confusion; the rest of the camera aperture is gathered from the finished image by a later pass, so this is what keeps the traced part from flickering rather than what sets the blur size. Each sample after the first costs one trace per pixel rather than a whole path.
caustica.options.rt.apertureMode.tooltip: Auto solves the f-number from the metered scene every frame; Manual pins it to the Aperture value, exactly like a lens ring. Wider apertures (small f-numbers) blur the background more and let in more light.
caustica.options.rt.aperture.tooltip: The f-number: the focal length divided by the entrance pupil diameter. Wider (smaller numbers) gives a shallower depth of field and a brighter image; narrower (larger numbers) keeps more of the scene in focus and darkens the image.
caustica.options.rt.shutterMode.tooltip: Auto solves the shutter time from the metered scene every frame; Manual pins it to the Shutter Time value.
caustica.options.rt.shutterTime.tooltip: How long the virtual shutter stays open. Longer times brighten the image (and, with Motion Blur on, lengthen the streak); shorter times darken it.
caustica.options.rt.focusMode.tooltip: Auto focuses on whatever the centre of the screen is pointing at, like a camera's centre autofocus point; Manual focuses at a fixed distance.
caustica.options.rt.focusDistance.toolti: How far from the camera the sharp plane sits, in metres. Everything at that distance stays sharp and everything nearer or farther blurs by an amount set by the aperture.
caustica.options.rt.frameGeneration.tool: Generates one interpolated frame between rendered frames for 2x output. Requires a supported NVIDIA GPU and driver.
caustica.options.rt.volumetricClouds.too: Draws the volumetric cloud deck and its shadows. Turning this off removes the cloud layer, its temporal pass, and cloud shadows from direct sunlight.
